name: Lesson 1.1: Atomic Orbitals & Electron Configuration
intro:
Atomic Orbitals & Quantum Numbers

Electrons reside in specific probability clouds called orbitals defined by four quantum numbers: principal (n), angular momentum (l), magnetic (ml), and spin (ms).

Key Principles:

  • Aufbau Principle: Electrons fill the lowest energy subshells first (1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, ...).
  • Pauli Exclusion Principle: No two electrons can have identical sets of four quantum numbers.
  • Hund's Rule: Orbitals of equal energy are each occupied by one electron before any orbital is doubly occupied.

name: Lesson 2.1: The Mole Concept & Balancing Chemical Equations
intro:
The Mole Concept & Stoichiometric Coefficients

One mole of any substance contains exactly 6.022 x 10^23 elementary entities (Avogadro's constant, N_A).

General Stoichiometry Workflow:

  1. Convert given mass (grams) to moles using molar mass: n = m / M.
  2. Use stoichiometric mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation.
  3. Convert calculated product moles back to desired units (grams, volume, or concentration).
